ANVIL 
Fixed hardened steel plates, usually welded to the cu tting table frame, between which the cutters pass 
and against which the cutters shear, tear or fracture the waste product. Anvils can be rebuilt to their 
original form. See Cutting Chamber picture below. 
 
AUTOMATIC LUBRICATION (AUTO-LUBE) SYSTEM 
A method of ensuring that selected components are alw ays adequately lubricated.  The system consists 
of an electric pump, one or more grease distribution valves, and several grease distribution lines. Wast e 
reducers are equipped with an Auto-Lube System for the cutter shaft bearings. 
 
AUTO REVERSE PROGRAM 
A pre-determined cutter sequence wherein the rotation direction of the cutter shaft is reversed periodically 
to agitate and redistribute the hopper contents. In dual shaft models, shaft reversals are staggered so that 
one shaft continues to operate in the normal directio n while the other shaft is reversing. All waste 
reducers are supplied with multiple factory-set Auto R everse Programs plus one that can be user-
configured.  
 
CHASSIS 
A large assembly, consisting of a fabricated frame wit h several access doors and covers onto which a 
Cutting Table, Discharge Conveyor, HPU, Control Panel  and Motor Starter Panel can be mounted or 
installed. A chassis can be converted into a mobile platform (see Semi-Trailer). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CLOSED-LOOP HYDRAULIC CIRCUIT 
A piping arrangement in which pump delivery, after pa ssing through other hydraulic components, by-
passes the reservoir and returns directly to pump inl et. Closed-Loop systems require smaller reservoirs, 
are more energy efficient, and are generally more compa ct than Open-Loop systems (see Open-Loop 
Hydraulic Circuit). 
 
CONTROL PANEL 
An electrical assembly, consisting of an enclosure that houses the PLC and a variety of other control 
components.

CUTTERS 
Specially shaped hardened steel plates that are an integral part of the cutter shaft.  Cutters have sever al 
hooks that grab waste material and pull it into and through the anvils, thus shredding, tearing and 
fracturing the material and effecting size reduction. C utters can be rebuilt to their original form. Cutter s 
come in four-hook (High Force) and six-hook (High Volume) styles. See below. 
 
CUTTER SHAFT 
The large rotating part within the cutting chamber th at consists of several cutters, cutter spacers, and an 
internal shaft.  Waste reducers are equipped with one or two cutter shafts. See below. 
 
CUTTER STYLE 
There are two styles of cutters available – High Force (HF) and High Volume (HV). HF cutters feature four 
hooks, two for each rotation direction, and are approp riate for processing more resistant waste material. 
HV cutters have six hooks, three for each rotation dir ection, have a larger sweep diameter, and are 
appropriate for processing less resistant waste material at a higher throughput rate.

CUTTING CHAMBER 
The zone that is occupied by the rotating cutter shafts and the anvils. 
 
 
 
 
 Cutter Shaft

CUTTING TABLE 
The large mechanical assembly in which waste reduction a ctually takes place. It includes a fabricated 
steel frame, one or two cutter shafts, several anvil s, the cutter shaft bearings, and one or more hydraul ic 
motors. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 TAIL END HEAD END 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CUTTING TABLE HEAD END 
The end of the cutting table where the hydraulic connections from the HPU are made. See above. 
 
CUTTING TABLE TAIL END 
The end of the cutting table away from where the hydra ulic connections from the HPU are made. See 
above.

DISCHARGE CONVEYOR 
A conveyor that carries away the processed waste materia l. A discharge conveyor may be either 
electrically or hydraulically driven, and may be a straight take-away conveyor, or a bent or folding load-out 
conveyor for elevated discharge. 
 
HOPPER 
The integral part of the cutting table into which waste material is fed or dumped. 
 
HOPPER EXTENSION 
One or more fabricated components that increase the cap acity of the hopper. On mobile systems, the 
hopper extension is typically removed during transport. 
 
HYDRAULIC POWER UNIT (HPU) 
An assembly powered by a diesel engine or one or more  electric motors and consisting of hydraulic 
pumps, a reservoir, hydraulic valves, a heat exchanger, and various hydraulic control devices.  
 
MOTOR STARTER PANEL 
An electrical assembly for HPUs powered by electric motor s. It consists of an enclosure that houses the 
main breaker, the contactors for supplying power to all  electric motors, various circuit protection and 
monitoring devices, and a control voltage power supply. 
 
OPEN-LOOP HYDRAULIC CIRCUIT 
A hydraulic circuit in which the pump inlet is connected to a reservoir and the pump outlet is connected to 
the motor inlet. The motor outlet is connected back to the reservoir. Motor rotation is started, stopped and 
reversed by a directional control valve (see Closed Loop Hydraulic Drive). 
 
PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC) 
A microprocessor-based control device that is factory pro grammed and directs such activities as cutter 
shaft rotation and speed, as well as monitoring numerous remote devices for potential fault conditions.  It 
is housed within the control panel. 
 
SEMI TRAILER 
Mobile waste reducers are mounted on specially designed Semi-Trailers. See below. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
STAND 
A mechanical structure upon which the cutter table is mo unted on stationary systems. On systems that 
include a discharge conveyor the stand may include an int egral discharge chute and a means of 
supporting the discharge conveyor.
